evidence: 2026-09-30: real signup through the Agent Vault proxy using this recipe (vault-minted password), with browser egress through the owner's tunnel on a US network. The email went into #username; for a new address the next step asked for first name, last name and a password (a pre-ticked checkbox was left as it was), and submit moved on to a subscribe offer. An email from accounts@noreply.theatlantic.com arrived at the signup address. A sign-in straight after was not accepted (the site stayed signed out). The account owner opened the verification link in that email, and a fresh sign-in with the same credentials then left theatlantic.com showing My Account.
gotchas: One page for both signing in and signing up: it asks for the email first and decides from it. A NEW address is then asked for a first name, last name and a password on the same step; a known address gets the password alone.
The box is named username but takes an email address.
The new-account step carries a pre-ticked checkbox (email offers); leave it or untick it, it is not required.
After signup the page moves to a subscription offer; the account exists, but a sign-in does not take until the address is verified by a link sent by email, which belongs to the account owner.

The sign-in password step can take several seconds to appear after the email is submitted, and pressing Enter in it did nothing on 2026-09-30; click the submit button. Signed in, the theatlantic.com header shows My Account instead of Sign In.
